stem.en: A parabolic dune stands in a steady wind from the west. Plants hold its two arms. Which description is right?

text.en: The bare nose moves east, and the arms trail to the west.

feedback.en: Yes. The arms are held, the nose moves on, so the arms point upwind.

text.en: The nose stays fixed, and the two arms move east past it.

feedback.en: This is backwards. Plants hold the arms, and the bare nose is what moves.

text.en: The nose faces west, and the arms point east like a barchan.

feedback.en: That is how barchan horns run. Plants hold these arms back, so they point west.

text.en: The arms point north and south, straight across the wind.

feedback.en: The arms lie along the wind. They are stretched out as the nose moves away.

explanation.en: On a parabolic dune, plants hold the two arms while the bare nose moves downwind. The arms are left behind, so they point upwind. A barchan is the reverse: its horns point downwind.

hints.en: Which part of this dune is bare and free to move?
